subject: Future Tech
title: Why Self-Driving Cars?
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Self-Driving Cars? usable.

hook.text: 1.35 million people die in car crashes every year. Human error causes 94% of them. What if we removed the human?

buildup.text: We text, drowse, and rage behind the wheel. Machines don't. A computer never blinks, drinks, or checks its phone.

discovery.text: Autonomy can watch every direction at once and react in milliseconds instead of human lag.

twist.text: But perfection is the enemy. One robot car crash makes global headlines.

climax.text: The real question isn't whether AVs are perfect. It's whether they're safer than us. The data says they already are.

punchline.text: The safest driver on the road might be no driver at all.

quiz.question: What percentage of car crashes are caused by human error?
